items.issue: The initial definition says PIES = classes an adversary can 'successfully submit.' Later in the same section, PIES is redefined as 'the subset of those candidate classes with ≥1 guardrail bypass in the cycle,' and CPS (= 217) is introduced as the full candidate pattern space. If 'successfully submit' means 'the entry point accepts the input,' then the initial definition matches CPS, not PIES. If it means 'the attack bypasses guardrails,' it matches the later PIES definition. The ambiguity is that the same term 'exposure surface' is used for both the initial PIES definition and, implicitly, for CPS when the text calls CPS 'the unique exposure surface.'

items.issue: The confidence statement holds only in the zero-event case; with one observed poisoned retrieval the 95% upper bound is ≈0.55%, above the 0.3% target the sample size is claimed to certify.

items.evidence: Quote EXACT in chapter-24.md §4.2 item 3: 'samples 1,000 retrievals per cycle (n ≈ 1,000 sized for the <0.3% target at 95% confidence; 0.001 resolution)'. Recomputed Clopper–Pearson bounds (Python, exact binomial): x=0, n=1000, one-sided 95% upper = 0.002991 = 0.299% ≈ 0.3% ✓ (rule of three ✓); x=1, one-sided 95% = 0.004735 = 0.473%; x=1, two-sided 95% upper = 0.005559 = 0.556% ≈ 0.55% — matches the finding's stated ≈0.55% (two-sided CP/Wilson ✓). Under every convention the 1-event bound (0.47–0.56%) exceeds the 0.3% target, so the sample-size claim holds only in the zero-event case ✓; '0.001 resolution' is granularity (1/1,000), not confidence ✓.

items.page_hint: Ch 18 §3.1 (hardware capacity mapping table) and the paragraph following the co-residency list
items.issue: Two problems in one table. (a) The column header "# fit on 8×H100" does not say whether the number is instances of that model alone on the pool or GPUs required per instance; the parentheticals mix both readings (the FP16 row's parenthetical is a per-GPU fit test, the 4-bit row's is an instance count). The co-residency list then places one 8-bit model in a pool whose row says 2 fit, with no note reconciling the two. (b) The 64 GB reserve that produces the 436 GB KV budget is introduced without explanation in this chapter; it is the difference between C = 17 and C = 9, so a reader cannot tell whether it is a safety margin, activation workspace, or a fragmentation allowance.
items.quoted_clause: | # fit on 8×H100 | ... | 1 (140 GB weights across the 8-GPU pool, ~17.5 GB/GPU under TP; with KV, the canonical 436 GB KV budget is used (640 − 140 − 64)) | ... | ~5 (canonical 436 GB KV budget reserved: (640−436)/35 = 5.83 → floor 5; ~18 by weights alone; the worked deployment below uses 2 copies)
items.fix_instruction: In Ch 18 §3.1 rename the column to '# instances on one 8×H100 pool (this model alone)' and add a note that the co-residency list below is the actual deployment; define the 64 GB reserve at first use (or cite the chapter that defines it) and state what it covers.
items.evidence: Quote found EXACT (3/3 segments) despite _triage=ABSENT. Table §3.1 verbatim: '| 70B dense FP16 | ... | 1 (140 GB weights across the 8-GPU pool, ~17.5 GB/GPU under TP; with KV, the canonical 436 GB KV budget is used (640 − 140 − 64)) |' and '| 70B 4-bit GGUF | ... | ~5 (canonical 436 GB KV budget reserved: (640−436)/35 = 5.83 → floor 5; ~18 by weights alone; the worked deployment below uses 2 copies) |'. Mixed readings confirmed: the 8-bit row's '2' is GPUs-per-instance (parenthetical '94.9 GB > 80 GB per GPU' + later 'Minimum placement is ⌈(70 + 24.89)/80⌉ = 2 GPUs') while FP16's '1' and 4-bit's '~5' are instance counts ('The ~5-copies figure counts only GPU-resident GGUF copies') — one header, two populations. Co-residency list places 'One 70B 8-bit dense (70 GB)' while the row says 2 fit, with no reconciling note. 64 GB never defined in ch18 (only uses: '(640 − 140 − 64)' and '640 − 350 − 64 = 226 GB, so C = ⌊226/24.89⌋ = 9'). Recomputed: 640−140−64 = 436 ✓; 436/24.89 = 17.52 → 17 ✓; 226/24.89 = 9.08 → 9 ✓; 64/640 = 10% ✓; (17−9)/17 = 47% ✓.
